answer: Hardware attestation caps how many agents one machine can register. Each new identity must present a signed quote from a secure chip, and the network counts identities per chip, allowing only a few. A Sybil operator cannot just tell a fable of a thousand separate agents; every extra name needs another physical device he must buy, power and keep online. Like a raven that can guard only so many nests, one box earns one small share of rewards, and the nectar of fake scale costs real hardware per fake.
